one_line: An English-language founder origin-story reel in which a former kindergarten and first-grade teacher explains why she wrote a 190-day at-home preschool ebook (Playing Preschool), then tours the printed pages and ends on a link card, with a 'Comment LEARN' call in the caption.

hook.visual: Frame 0.0 s is a washed-out, blurred fade-in of the presenter with a burned-in caption; at 2 s a photo of an adult crouching with three small children in a waiting hall, at 4 s a family selfie of two adults and three young children against a green wall.
hook.on_screen_text: Back when I had three (burned-in caption, first word highlighted blue)
hook.first_spoken_line: Back when I had three kids, three and under,
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: 'three kids, three and under' is an instantly relatable chaos signal for parents, and the photos at 2 to 4 s show real family footage immediately; the first frame itself is faded and weak, so the opening works mainly through the spoken line.

beats.observed: Fade-in of the presenter, then two family photos (adult with three small children in a ferry-terminal-like waiting hall; family selfie). Burned-in captions with key words highlighted in blue.
beats.spoken: Back when I had three kids, three and under, I started looking into preschool options for my son.
beats.on_screen_text: Back when I had three / I started looking into preschool / options for my son.

beats.observed: Presenter in a white kitchen, black puff-sleeve top, hands clasped on the counter, speaking to camera with a to-camera caption stream.
beats.spoken: I was stunned at the cost and started doing some quick math, realizing that sending each of my kids to a few years of preschool, even just part time, was going to cost my family a staggering amount of money. This wasn't going to work for us.

beats.spoken: So I decided to look online for some at-home preschool options. I found worksheets, workbooks, computer programs, and other loosely written lessons, but nothing was as thorough or hands-on as I knew preschool at home could be.

payoff: The product reveal comes at about 36 s (cover shown), the credentials and customer proof by about 46 s, and the full contents and page tour between about 46 and 80 s; the closing link card is at about 86 s.
cta: In the video: an end card 'LEARN MORE AT' with a web address. In the caption: 'Comment LEARN and I'll send you more information' or follow the profile link. The spoken script has no CTA beyond 'I can't wait to introduce it to you'.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: the keyword 'Comment LEARN' in the caption gives people a one-word action that fits an automated reply flow, which fits the 2,334 comments; the cost-of-preschool problem is also a parent-to-parent talking point. I did not observe any DM flow, so this is not verified.
why_it_worked: 1,366,837 views vs a median of 248,562 (5.5x) on an 87-second video, with visuals changing every few seconds between presenter, family photos, product flat-lays and customer screenshots.
2,334 comments on 9,719 likes (comments about 24% of likes, an unusually high ratio) lines up with the caption keyword gate; like rate 0.71% is above the paid-promo range.

The structure runs problem (cost shock), failed alternatives, credential (former teacher photo), product reveal, social proof, tour of the actual printed pages, then a link card: every claim has a matching visual.
paid_signal: unclear, like_rate_pct 0.71 does not indicate paid reach by itself, but this is a direct product pitch with a keyword CTA, so a boosted post is possible; nothing in the frames confirms either way.

solo_route.how: 1) Get a founder voice memo or 60-second talking-head take telling the real reason LumeBook exists, plus 3 to 4 personal photos. 2) In CapCut build a burned-in caption stream with key words highlighted in the brand color and alternate the founder with photo cutaways every few seconds. 3) Film a flat-lay of a printed LumeBook (cover, a few spreads, the child's name on a page) and a screenshot collage of real customer messages, with permission. 4) End on a link card and add a 'comment BOOK' keyword to the caption.
solo_route.needs: The founder's true origin story and permission to use their photos; permission to show real customer messages; a printed sample of the book for the flat-lay. No kids needed.

lumebook_version.concept: A 45 to 60 second founder origin story with captions, intercut with a flat-lay tour of a printed LumeBook (cover, name page, a spread) and two real customer messages, ending on a link card and a 'comment' keyword in the caption. The origin story itself must come from the founder, not be invented.

evidence_notes: Observed: presenter, photos, flat-lays, customer message screenshots, table of contents, end card and burned-in captions. The English transcript is clean and matches the burned-in captions line by line. I did not identify any person from the frames; the caption (first person) and the account name are the only identity evidence, and I treat the photos as the narrator's family only because the narration says 'three kids' and the caption says 'I had a baby, a 2-year-old, and a 3-year-old'. Claims such as 'one of the most used preschool programs available' and 'for the last seven years' are spoken, not verifiable from the video. Table of contents rows and customer messages are small; only the legible text was transcribed and the rest is [unclear]. The Playing Preschool web address on the end card is partly covered by a blue bar and I did not read it with confidence. Video duration is 87.5 s per frames/index.json. I cannot hear music.
